items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.summary:

[...] It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress.

The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. Tôi có thể thực hiện các chức năng sau:

1. **Gửi câu hỏi**: Hỏi người dùng để làm rõ thông tin cần thiết.
2. **Lấy bài đăng gần đây**: Truy cập và lấy các bài đăng từ tài khoản mạng xã hội.
3. **Tìm kiếm trên mạng xã hội**: Tìm kiếm thông tin theo từ khóa trên các nền tảng mạng xã hội.

7. **Gửi đoạn văn bản**: Gửi nội dung văn bản đi.
8. **Tìm trong tài liệu nội bộ**: Tìm kiếm thông tin trong các tài liệu nội bộ theo truy vấn.
9. **Tìm bài báo khoa học**: Tìm kiếm và lấy thông tin về các bài báo khoa học.
10. **Lấy nội dung bài báo**: Truy cập và lấy nội dung văn bản từ một bài báo khoa học.
11. **Lọc danh sách tin**: Lọc các tin đã có theo từ khóa trong tiêu đề hoặc tóm tắt.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Robotics | Definition, Components, Unimate, Applications, & Facts | Britannica
items.summary:
Robotics is the design, construction, and use of machines, called robots, to perform tasks traditionally carried out by humans. Robots may use sensors that provide abilities resembling vision, touch, or temperature sensing, while control systems direct movements and actions. Some robots also employ artificial intelligence and machine learning, allowing them to make simple decisions, adapt to changing conditions, and operate with increasing independence.

### Who coined the term robot? [...] Robotics, design, construction, and use of machines (robots) to perform tasks done traditionally by human beings. Robots are widely used in such industries as automobile manufacturing to perform simple repetitive tasks and in industries where work must be performed in environments hazardous to humans. Many aspects of robotics involve artificial intelligence (AI); robots may be equipped with the equivalent of human senses such as vision, touch, and the ability to sense temperature. Some are [...] Robotics research continues to focus on improving autonomy, adaptability, and human-robot interaction. Advances in machine learning, computer vision, and sensor technology are expected to expand the use of robots in health care, logistics, environmental monitoring, and elder care.
